source_issues.detail: Source says combined defense rows are 100%, contradicting its statement that no defense is perfect. Layering does not imply a total guarantee. Exact confidence/coverage/latency claims lack evaluation setup. All claims retained as frozen source, not endorsed.

Source inconsistently says Moderation has 11 versus 13 categories; unlimited usage/no-rate-limits are unconditional product claims that require current verification. No live verification under English-only frozen scope.

LlamaGuard model versions, sizes and category counts differ across sections (3 1B/8B/7B versus 4 2B/8B; 13 versus 14). General content-safety classification is presented as a dedicated prompt-injection detector. All names/numbers retained, not corrected or verified.

detect_injection lowercases text but several regex literals retain uppercase DAN, INST or system-marker casing. They can fail to match. Encoding-evasion confidence is 0.70, below rejection threshold 0.75, so encoding flag alone passes. Code is unchanged.

PII regex re.findall can return capturing-group values rather than full phone/DOB matches, so recorded value hashes may not represent the detected full value. Broad regexes also lack validation and can produce false positives/negatives. Unchanged.

Example relevance/hallucination checks use token overlap, not factual verification or embeddings. High overlap can coexist with wrong negation or $50,000 versus $500. Empty meaningful word sets pass. The numerical example is explained but no factual-balance checker is implemented. Preserved.

Demo All blocked uses all(True for ... if blocked), which returns True even when some or all attacks pass, and processes all attacks a second time. This is not a valid all-attacks-blocked assertion. Retained unchanged.
Languages metadata is Python, but code/main.ts also exists; frozen metadata retained per task instructions.

Lesson objectives/diagram mention hallucinated URLs and rate limiting absent from the implemented pipeline (rate limiter is left as an exercise); last reading refers to a human-in-the-loop escalation pattern not developed in the lesson. Source prose retained.

Unconditional attack timeline, historical attributions, model/tool support and availability, fixed latency/accuracy, PII counts and language counts, canary success implication, three-category taxonomy versus five-row table, and cost recommendations are time-sensitive or oversimplified source assertions. None were externally verified or silently fixed.
GuardrailMonitor.summary empty-event shape lacks total_requests, while print_dashboard indexes it. Unchanged; not exercised.
